response.goal: Fix the n8n workflow so the full file of about 5,000 rows lands every night in Google Sheets without failing due to rate limits, including retries and a Slack message if it still fails.

plan.step: Analyze the existing n8n workflow and Google Sheets node configuration to identify the rate limit (429) trigger points during the 5,000 row import.
Implement batching or rate-limiting logic within the n8n workflow to handle large data imports without exceeding Google Sheets API limits.
Configure built-in error handling and automatic retry mechanisms for the Google Sheets node inside the n8n workflow.
Add a Slack notification node to alert the team if the workflow still fails after retries.

milestones.name: Diagnostic and Fix Implementation
milestones.deliverable: Updated n8n workflow with batching, rate-limit handling, and retries.

milestones.name: Testing and Slack Alert Integration
milestones.deliverable: Fully tested import of the 5,000 row CSV and verified Slack failure alerts.

risks.risk: Google Sheets API write quotas might still restrict high-frequency batch requests even with throttling.
risks.mitigation: Implement structured delays between batch chunks or switch to appending rows in optimized larger arrays rather than individual requests.

risks.risk: The CSV structure or source file format may have changed causing parsing issues alongside the rate limit.
risks.mitigation: Inspect the raw CSV input structure prior to running test imports.

questions: What is the exact structure of the incoming CSV file and how is it currently being read into n8n?
Which Slack channel should the failure alert notifications be sent to?
assumptions: The client has provided or will provide access to the existing n8n instance and Google Sheets document.
The client has a Slack workspace set up where the webhook or integration app can post failure messages.
